name: Comparisons
expr: (lambda M: (lambda xs: (lambda meds: [len(meds), meds[:4], meds[-1], sum(meds), comparisons() <= 6 * len(xs) * __import__('math').log2(len(xs))])([(M.add(x), float(M.median()))[1] for x in xs]))(counted(args[0])))(MedianFinder())
show: add 3,000 values, asking for the median after each: [how many, first four, last, sum, at most 6 n log₂ n comparisons?]
why: Each add moves a value through a heap or two: O(log n) comparisons. Keeping one list sorted with a scan, or sorting after each add, costs O(n) comparisons per add, millions in total here.

name: 50,000 values

show: add 50,000 values with a median after each: the last three medians
why: O(log n) per add and O(1) per median. If this timed out, the median may be computed by sorting or scanning.
